hypothesis: The file-create module writes only the bounded sector set for the 512 MiB region test file on the 62.5 GB card, after a 326-sector read-only backup.
prediction:
The card has one FAT32 partition from sector 32,768 (122,105,856 sectors): 64 sectors per cluster, 64 reserved sectors, two FATs of 14,912 sectors, FSInfo at partition sector 1, root cluster 2, 1,907,437 clusters, an empty root directory (read on 2026-11-02). The module's plan on a model volume of this geometry made by mkfs.fat with the same parameters, for a file of 536,870,912 bytes (16,384 clusters):
| Set | Absolute sectors | Count | Written |
| Data, clusters 3 to 16,386 | 62,720 to 1,111,295 | 1,048,576 | all |
| FAT copy 1, indexes 0 to 128 | 32,832 to 32,960 | 129 | all |
| FAT copy 2, indexes 0 to 128 | 47,744 to 47,872 | 129 | all |
| FSInfo | 32,769 | 1 | 1 |
| Root directory cluster 2 | 62,656 to 62,719 | 64 | sector 62,656 (slots 0 to 3) |
Nothing else is allowed: not the boot sector (32,768), its backup (32,774), the backup FSInfo (32,775), the rest of either FAT, any other cluster, and nothing below sector 32,768. The exact slots follow from the directory read at run time; the allowed root sectors are the 64 of the cluster.
Backup plan: a read-only lifetime (the probe's mode, read-only core) returns the bytes of every sector the create may change or whose neighbour it may confuse, in one payload, and the host keeps them with their SHA-256:
| Sectors | Count |
| Boot sector 32,768, backup boot 32,774, FSInfo 32,769, backup FSInfo 32,775 | 4 |
| FAT copy 1, 32,832 to 32,960 | 129 |
| FAT copy 2, 47,744 to 47,872 | 129 |
| Root directory cluster, 62,656 to 62,719 | 64 |
That is 326 sectors, 166,912 bytes. The data clusters need no backup: they are free space on a volume with no file. The write lifetimes carry the backup's SHA-256 in their input, read the same sectors again before the first write and refuse to write unless the hash matches. Restore writes the backed-up FAT, FSInfo and root sectors back (the same bounded sets without the data extent); afterwards every sector outside the data extent equals the backup, and the data clusters keep the generated bytes but are free space again.
Write speed: the PIO core writes one sector per CMD24 with a CMD13 after it; at 0.5 to 1.5 ms per sector the 1,048,576 data sectors take 9 to 26 minutes, beyond one probe session (at most 600 s); the phased module allows several data lifetimes of about 8 minutes each; a CMD25 multiple-block write would cut that to a few minutes. The first write lifetime should measure the rate on a small slice (for example 16 MiB of the data extent). Generation cost: the stream (counter-mode SHA-256 of tools/region_test_file.py) costs one SHA-256 compression per 32 bytes, about 50 cycles per byte, about 10 MB/s at the probe's 494 MHz and 54 s for the whole file, overlapped with nothing in a PIO write. The directory entry carries the fixed date 2026-11-02 and time 00:00:00.
conclusion: Not run through this module. The board wrote the file with the general write service instead (CMD25 with descriptor DMA, entries 1793623788842205312-60954030 and 1793632378497932347-1618d4a8): a 512 MiB file in a contiguous chain from cluster 47 to 16430, measured at 14.7 MB/s flushed, against the 9 to 26 minutes predicted for the PIO path. The runner admits bounded writes through its --storage-write path with a blob of allowed ranges and the backup hash.
narrative: The module was checked on the host only (record region-test-file-write-host-checks). The first plan wrote into the root directory's first cluster; the write service creates /sunstone-test/sunstone-region-test.bin in a directory instead.

hypothesis: fat32_create writes only the bounded set, in order, and leaves a consistent volume that fsck.fat accepts.
narrative: checks/fat32-create.py creates the file on mkfs.fat images (512-byte and 4 KiB clusters, one inside a card image at sector 32,768, with and without other files, exact and inexact cluster multiples) and requires: fsck.fat -n clean before and after; every written sector inside the bounded set the Python side computes from the geometry, in the required order; the file read back by an independent Python parser with the right digest, and the chain equal in both FATs; a consistent volume (FSInfo equal to the counted free clusters, FATs equal); the guard's allowed set equal to the geometry, and sectors next to it refused; restore returning every sector outside the data extent; the same image from six phased calls as from one. Refusals, each with no write: a first cluster in the root directory, past the volume, a cluster count of the whole volume, slots outside the root cluster, a chain entry or slot that changed after the plan, a volume without a contiguous free run, an existing name, a full root cluster. A write that fails part way before the chain leaves a clean volume. mtools is not installed on the host, so the independent parser stands in for it.
